items.summary: Plants are sessile organisms exposed to a constant dialogue with various pests, insects, and microbes. After communication through various interactions (mutualism, predation, and parasitism), the plants trigger a range of volatile organic compounds (VOCs) through the modulation of the host gene. items.title: A biosynthetic paradox implicating dynamic zeaxanthin biosynthesis at the ER-LD interface
items.summary: Traditional metabolic engineering often treats lipid droplets (LDs) as inert storage sinks and assumes shortening enzyme-substrate distance inherently enhances pathway efficiency. Harnessing Yarrowia lipolytica for zeaxanthin production, we uncovered a pivotal “spatial paradox” challenging this conventional dogma. A selective shielding strategy first identified the hydroxylase Pa CrtZ as the primary biosynthetic bottleneck. items.title: Female Melanostoma hoverflies pollinate Cypripedium yatabeanum through a Paphiopedilum ‐like floral trap
items.summary: Societal Impact Statement Conserving rare plants requires understanding the ecological interactions that enable their reproduction. Most studied Cypripedium species are pollinated by bees, but the pollinators of many slipper orchids remain undocumented. We show that Cypripedium yatabeanum is pollinated by female aphidophagous hoverflies despite sharing broadly similar floral architecture with the closely related, bee‐pollinated Cypripedium guttatum . This contrast indicates that pollinators cannot be inferred from floral structure alone. items.title: A Smelly Conflict: The Role of Olfactory Information in the Interaction of Insect Herbivores and Their Natural Enemies
items.summary: ABSTRACT Chemical communication is one of the most fundamental ways in which insects interact with their environment. Many herbivores rely on olfactory cues such as plant volatiles to locate natural‐enemy‐free spaces for feeding or ovipositing; conversely, predatory and parasitic natural enemies detect herbivores by chemical cues from damaged plants or from the herbivores themselves. The role olfactory cues play in mediating insect behaviors as well as the molecular and neuronal mechanisms by which these infochemicals are perceived have been investigated in a wide range of insects. Metabolic engineering of yeast historically relied on a narrow set of reference species and strains, especially Saccharomyces cerevisiae. Recent studies, however, show that applying identical pathway designs to different strain backgrounds or species can yield significant differences in titer, rate and yield (TRY). items.summary: The present study employs global transcriptional engineering (GTE) to optimize metabolic flux toward linalool synthesis by screening seven key transcription factors in Saccharomyces cerevisiae. items.summary: Herbivore-induced plant volatiles (HIPVs) are critical mediators of tritrophic interactions, providing parasitoids with reliable cues for host location and parasitisation. items.summary: Friedelin (FD) is a pentacyclic triterpenoid with significant pharmacological potential and serves as the biosynthetic precursor to the anti-obesity drug celastrol. This article critically reviews the state-of-the-art in FD research, spanning natural distribution, extraction methodologies, and the molecular basis of its biosynthesis. items.title: Closing the loop on precision fermentation: recycling and upcycling spent media and biomass
items.summary: Precision fermentation (PF) offers a flexible method for producing high-value food ingredients, but it generates large volumes of spent media and microbial biomass, which pose environmental and economic challenges. This article explores strategies for recycling spent media into fresh fermentation inputs and upcycling microbial biomass into food ingredients. Focusing on yeast and fungal fermentations, we examine case studies involving widely-used chassis strains. Case studies indicate that recycling can reduce wastewater emissions by 70% or more, and reduce operating cost by nearly 30%. items.title: Chloroplast genome engineering: Recent advances, pathways towards commercialization and future directions
items.summary: Chloroplasts are ideal biofactories because thousands of transgene copies integrated into each plant cell to produce high levels of recombinant proteins and enzymes. Nuclear genome engineering ushered in the GMO revolution for crop protection that mostly required lower levels of transgene expression. Higher level expression and biosafety through gene containment facilitate new applications of GM crops, including production of high-value biopharmaceuticals and enzymes. items.summary: The spotted lanternfly (Lycorma delicatula [White]), an invasive fulgorid planthopper of significant economic concern, relies on a complex suite of chemical signals to navigate host selection, aggregation, and reproductive success in its US invaded range.
